newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Sao Paulo court delays CVRD appeal hearing.
newsitem.headline: Sao Paulo court delays CVRD appeal hearing.

text.p: A court in Sao Paulo has delayed a hearing on the Brazilian government's appeal of an injunction against the privatization of Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) until May 5 at the earliest, a court official said on Tuesday.

An aide to the presiding judge on the Sao Paulo Regional Federal Tribunal said the judge had canceled a special session of the court called to hear the government's appeal of an injunction granted on Friday.
"We did not have a quorum for the session. The earliest date now to hear the case is May 5," the aide said.
It was not immediately clear whether the government could go over the head of the Sao Paulo tribunal and appeal to a higher court, he said.

Officials at the Planning Ministry and the National Development Bank (BNDES) have said the Sao Paulo injunction is the most troubling of a host of court orders that delayed the Tuesday's scheduled start of the CVRD sell-off.
Forty-five percent of the mining company's voting shares had been due to be auctioned at 1000 local time (1300 GMT).
The presiding judge in Sao Paulo, Jorge Scartezzini, has already rejected at least one government appeal.
Newspapers said Tuesday that the injunction was also the most difficult to revoke because it had been granted at the instigation of several of the country's leading jurists.

Planning Minister Antonio Kandir and Jose Pio Borges, the development banks's privatization director, were holding talks with government lawyers in Rio. Luiz Carlos Mendonca de Barros, president of the bank, was in the Brazilian capital of Brasilia.
Mendonca de Barros on Monday said the bank would continue trying to appeal injunctions against the CVRD sale until 1700 local (2000 GMT) Tuesday.
